## Prerequisites

```powershell
Install-Module ExchangeOnlineManagement -Scope CurrentUser
Connect-IPPSSession   # Security & Compliance PowerShell
```

## Step 1 — the four-tier label taxonomy (Book 09's CUI mapping)

```powershell
New-Label -Name "Public"        -DisplayName "Public"        -Tooltip "Approved for release"
New-Label -Name "Internal"      -DisplayName "Internal"      -Tooltip "Business data, not for release"
New-Label -Name "CUI-Basic"     -DisplayName "CUI Basic"     -Tooltip "NARA CUI Registry - basic" `
          -EncryptionEnabled $true -EncryptionProtectionType Template
New-Label -Name "CUI-Specified" -DisplayName "CUI Specified" -Tooltip "NARA CUI Registry - specified" `
          -EncryptionEnabled $true -EncryptionProtectionType Template

# Publish EVERYWHERE from day one — Book 09's first pitfall is single-location publishing
New-LabelPolicy -Name "AAN-Lab-Labels" -Labels "Public","Internal","CUI-Basic","CUI-Specified" `
                -ExchangeLocation All -SharePointLocation All -OneDriveLocation All
```

## Step 2 — custom SIT + DLP in simulation mode

A corroborated custom SIT (pattern + keyword) and a DLP policy that starts
in **simulation**, per Book 09's discipline:

```powershell
# Custom SIT: employee ID "EMP" + 9 digits, corroborated by a keyword
$rulePack = New-DlpSensitiveInformationTypeRulePackage -FileData ([byte[]](Get-Content .\emp-sit.xml -Encoding Byte))

New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Name "AAN-Lab-CUI-DLP" -Mode TestWithNotifications `
    -ExchangeLocation All -SharePointLocation All -OneDriveLocation All
New-DlpComplianceRule -Name "Block external CUI share" -Policy "AAN-Lab-CUI-DLP" `
    -ContentContainsSensitiveInformation @{Name="U.S. Social Security Number (SSN)"; minCount="1"} `
    -BlockAccess $true -BlockAccessScope PerUser -NotifyUser Owner
```

Seed SharePoint with test documents containing fake SSNs (`078-05-1120`
style test values), wait for the simulation report, and review false
positives **before** switching `-Mode` to `Enforce` — mislabeling at scale
is the pitfall Book 09 calls out.

## Step 3 — Key Vault Premium + rotating CMK

```bash
az group create -n rg-aan-purview-lab -l eastus
az keyvault create -n kv-aan-lab-$RANDOM -g rg-aan-purview-lab --sku premium \
    --enable-purge-protection true --enable-rbac-authorization true
az keyvault key create --vault-name <vault> -n cmk-sql-tde --kty RSA-HSM --size 2048
az keyvault key rotation-policy update --vault-name <vault> -n cmk-sql-tde --value '{
  "lifetimeActions": [{"trigger": {"timeBeforeExpiry": "P30D"}, "action": {"type": "Rotate"}}],
  "attributes": {"expiryTime": "P12M"}
}'
```

Optional extension: point an Azure SQL test server's TDE protector at the
key (`az sql server tde-key set --server-key-type AzureKeyVault`) and
confirm key operations land in the vault's diagnostic logs — Book 09's
AU-12-vs-AU-10 distinction made concrete.

## Bind the evidence

Three artifacts: the label policy export
(`Get-LabelPolicy | ConvertTo-Json`), the DLP simulation report, and the
vault's key-rotation policy JSON. Together they evidence the MP/SC-12/28
closures Book 09 claims; score against the
[slot 4 rubric](../assessment-rubrics.html#slot-4).

## Teardown

```powershell
Remove-DlpCompliancePolicy -Identity "AAN-Lab-CUI-DLP"
Remove-LabelPolicy -Identity "AAN-Lab-Labels"
"Public","Internal","CUI-Basic","CUI-Specified" | ForEach-Object { Remove-Label -Identity $_ }
```

```bash
az group delete -n rg-aan-purview-lab --yes --no-wait   # purge-protected vault ages out on its own
```
